classification.difficultyReason: Combine exact special-triangle side ratios with a perimeter equation and rationalise a binomial surd denominator.

content.prompt: A piece of wire 20 cm long is bent in the shape of a triangle with interior angles $30^\circ$, $60^\circ$ and $90^\circ$. Find the length of the hypotenuse, giving your answer in surd form with a rational denominator.

answer.worked:
Let the hypotenuse be $h$ cm. The exact $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ ratios give the other sides as $\dfrac h2$ cm and $\dfrac{\sqrt3h}{2}$ cm.

The wire forms the perimeter, so
$$\begin{align*}h+\frac h2+\frac{\sqrt3h}{2}&=20\\h(3+\sqrt3)&=40\\h&=\frac{40}{3+\sqrt3}\\h&=\frac{40(3-\sqrt3)}{(3+\sqrt3)(3-\sqrt3)}\\h&=\frac{40(3-\sqrt3)}{6}\\h&=\frac{20(3-\sqrt3)}{3}.\end{align*}$$
The hypotenuse is $\dfrac{20(3-\sqrt3)}{3}\text{ cm}$.
